detail.longDescription: How can map_windows preserve state after None ? #![feature(iter_map_windows)] let mut n = 0; let iter = std::iter::from_fn(move || { let x = n; n += 1; (x != 3).then_some(x) }); let mut windows = iter.map_windows(|&[a, b]| (a, b)); assert_eq!(windows.next(), Some((0, 1))); assert_eq!(windows.next(), Some((1, 2))); assert_eq!(windows.next(), None); assert_eq!(windows.next(), Some((4, 5))); // wanted (2, 4) map_windows resets after a non-fused iterator returns None . Is there an adapter that preserves the partial window, or is this impossible because None cannot distinguish a temporary gap from permanent exhaustion?
